subject: Mid-cycle expansion: payment schedule & discount options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Rios <sam.rios@novaplc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle expansion: payment schedule & discount options

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Nova is ready to add an additional 250k token-months of capacity mid-contract. To make the amendment straightforward, I ran two practical payment/discount options for your procurement team to consider: 

Option A — Annualize and apply uplift discount
- Add the 250k as an annualized top-up to the existing commitment; invoice pro-rated portion for the remainder of the current term, then annual billing thereafter.
- Commercial tradeoff: 5% uplift discount on the incremental commit if Nova signs and accepts the amendment within this quarter.

Option B — Midterm top-up, net60 billing
- Bill the incremental usage as a mid-cycle invoice (pro-rated for days remaining) on net60 terms, no prepay required.
- Commercial tradeoff: standard pricing with a 3% discount available if Nova agrees to net60 + commit confirmation.

I've attached a draft quote (quote_NOVA-8342_v1.pdf) that shows the math across both options. Quick asks:
- Which payment cadence would your finance team prefer (annualize with prepay vs net60 midterm invoice)?
- Any mandate around co-terming with your existing renewal date (we can co-term the amendment to align with your Jan 1 renewal or keep it as an add-on)?

If you want, Ben and Marissa are on copy to confirm billing mechanics and discount gates. Happy to jump on a quick call to finalize.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: quote_NOVA-8342_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Sam Rios <sam.rios@novaplc.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novaplc.com
Date: 2027-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle expansion: payment schedule & discount options

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying items from finance/procurement: 
1) For Option A (annualize) — is the 5% applied only to the incremental 250k or to our full commitment after the amendment?
2) For Option B (net60) — can you confirm whether the pro-rate for the mid-cycle invoice will show as a separate line item (we need that for our AP reconciliation)?
3) Co-term: our renewal is Jan 1 and procurement strongly prefers everything co-termed where possible.

Ideally we would avoid prepaying a full year today. If you can do a clear pro-rated midterm invoice and lock the 5% discount across the incremental commit (even if we keep the payment net60), that would help move this quickly. Also our procurement team would like Net60 on the invoice.

Copying procurement for final confirmation. If you can send me a revised amendment that reflects: (a) pro-rated midterm invoice line, (b) discount applied to incremental commit only, and (c) co-term to Jan 1 — we can push this through our approvals next week.

Thanks,
Sam Rios
Head of Product Operations, Nova PLC
sam.rios@novaplc.com

Procurement: procurement@novaplc.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Rios <sam.rios@novaplc.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle expansion: payment schedule & discount options

On Sun, May 16, 2027 at 11:03 AM Sam Rios <sam.rios@novaplc.com> wrote:
> Marcus —
> 
> Appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying items from finance/procurement: 
> 1) For Option A (annualize) — is the 5% applied only to the incremental 250k or to our full commitment after the amendment?
> 2) For Option B (net60) — can you confirm whether the pro-rate for the mid-cycle invoice will show as a separate line item (we need that for our AP reconciliation)?
> 3) Co-term: our renewal is Jan 1 and procurement strongly prefers everything co-termed where possible.

Sam — thanks for the questions. High level answers and the tradeoffs: 
- Discount scope: we can limit the 5% to the incremental 250k only (simpler for your internal reporting), or extend it to the full post-amendment annualized commitment if Nova is willing to prepay for the year. So 5% incremental-only (no prepay), or 5% on full commitment (requires annual prepay).
- Invoice presentation: Marissa will confirm, but standard practice is to show a separate prorated line item for the midterm top-up and then the recurring annualized commit on the subsequent invoices. That satisfies AP and makes reconciliation straightforward.
- Co-term to Jan 1: we can co-term. If we co-term, the incremental portion will be pro-rated to the Jan 1 horizon and then folded into the annual commit after Jan 1.

Recommended path to close quickly: 
1) Send amendment that co-terms to Jan 1, shows a separate prorated midterm line, and applies a 3% discount for net60 payment terms on the incremental 250k.
2) Offer an early-sign window: if Nova signs the amendment and elects the annualize/prepay route within 10 business days, convert to a 5% incremental discount instead and issue a credit for the difference on the first annual invoice.

If that sounds acceptable, Marissa can generate the amendment draft and the finance-friendly invoice layout. 

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Rios <sam.rios@novaplc.com>, procurement@novaplc.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle expansion: payment schedule & discount options

Hi Sam / procurement —

Confirming billing ops side and next steps: 
- We will present a separate prorated invoice line for the mid-cycle 250k top-up showing exact pro-rate dates and per-unit calculations for AP.
- Co-term: amendment will be drafted to co-term to Jan 1, 2028. The mid-cycle prorated amount will be billed on the next invoice cycle (net60 as requested) and the post-Jan-1 portion will roll into the annualized commitment.
- Discount mechanics: we can implement Ben's suggestion (3% at net60 on the incremental commit) and an early-sign conversion to 5% (we will auto-apply a credit to the first annual invoice).

I've attached a working amendment draft (amendment_draft_NOVA-8342.docx) that reflects the billing line-item format procurement prefers. Please flag any redlines; if we get a signed amendment by close of business Friday we can have the first prorated invoice issued on next Tuesday's billing run.

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
